cells.tense: You're here, with your hands on it, and you know what you're keeping alive.
cells.verb: tending what grows, one careful choice at a time
cells.place: in the place where you decide what gets your attention
cells.ask: Let one thing you've been tending be seen as finished — show someone what it took, and then set it down.
cells.core:
You're here, with your hands on it, and you know what you're keeping alive. Two things are pulling on you and you haven't dropped either one — you've chosen them both, and you keep choosing them, in small daily acts of care rather than big declarations. That's what direction looks like when it's working: not a speech about what matters, but the watering done on time.

Something this steady can afford to be seen. One thing you've grown is probably close to done. Let someone look at it, let them know what it cost you, and let it be finished — set down what's complete, so your hands are free for what's next.
cells.sheetLine: You tend what you chose, and the tending is the choosing.

cells.tense: You're already living in the season where it all goes wrong if you look away.
cells.verb: tending what grows, one careful choice at a time
cells.place: in the place where you decide what gets your attention
cells.ask: Picture one of these already grown — fully done, nothing left to manage — and let yourself feel finished with it for a minute.
cells.core:
You're already living in the season where it all goes wrong if you look away. So you don't look away. Every choice about where your energy goes is really a choice to check on something again, adjust something again, make sure. The care is real. But it's been running so far ahead of what's actually growing that the growing can't be felt — you're too busy protecting a harvest that hasn't come.

The way back isn't less care. It's letting yourself imagine one thing you're tending as already grown — complete, satisfying, nothing more to do — and staying there long enough to feel it. Care that can picture its own ending stops clutching, and holds instead.
cells.sheetLine: You're guarding what's growing so hard it can't be felt growing.

cells.tense: You chose this once, a while back, and you're still standing at the moment you chose it.
cells.verb: tending what grows, one careful choice at a time
cells.place: in the place where you decide what gets your attention
cells.ask: Say out loud what you were hoping for when you started this — and keep saying it, especially on the days it feels foolish.
cells.core:
You chose this once, a while back, and you're still standing at the moment you chose it. The choice was real. The tending that was supposed to follow it thinned out somewhere — the daily attention, the small adjustments, the showing up — and now the thing is still technically yours and mostly untended. You can see the door you walked through; you just haven't walked much further.

Don't try to force the care back by discipline. Go to what's underneath it: what you were hoping for when you started. Say it, to yourself or to someone, and keep saying it after everything that's happened since. Hope that stays spoken pulls attention back behind it, and the tending starts again without being pushed.
cells.sheetLine: You chose it and stopped tending it; the hope is where the care comes back in.

cells.tense: You're already doing it; you just talk about it as if it's happening to you.
cells.verb: tending what grows, one careful choice at a time
cells.place: in the place where you decide what gets your attention
cells.ask: Tell one person what one of these things has cost you, plainly, and let it count as something you gave rather than something you owed.
cells.core:
You're already doing it; you just talk about it as if it's happening to you. Things around you are staying alive because you keep them alive — you've picked them, you give them your attention, you keep two of them going at once without dropping either. But ask you and it's just keeping up, just obligations, just what anyone would do. The direction is set and the care is steady and the one person not crediting it is you.

The simplest way back is to let what you've given be seen. Tell someone what one of these has cost you — not as a complaint, as a fact — and let it land as yours. Care that's acknowledged can let things finish; care that's disowned just keeps going without ever getting to set anything down.
cells.sheetLine: You're already tending this on purpose. You've been calling it keeping up.
